The '''1983–84 season''' was '''[[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid Club de Fútbol]]'s''' [[List of Real Madrid CF seasons|82nd season]] in existence and the club's [[La Liga records and statistics#All-time La Liga table|53rd consecutive season]] in the top flight of Spanish football.

==Summary==
This season is best remembered for the debut of popular young playmaker [[Emilio Butragueño]]<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.marca.com/2014/02/05/futbol/equipos/real_madrid/1391598284.html|publisher=Diario Marca|title=30 years of Butragueño debut|language=es|accessdate=2 July 2020|date=5 February 1984}}</ref> and his "[[La Quinta del Buitre]]" (Chendo, Sanchis, Martín Vázquez, Pardeza and Michel)<ref>{{cite web|url=https://elpais.com/diario/1984/12/01/deportes/470703610_850215.html|work=El País|title=Amancio, the man who discovered La Quinta del Buitre|language=es|accessdate=2 July 2020|date=1 December 1984}}</ref> a group of teenage players climbing from its reserve team [[Real Madrid Castilla|Castilla]] towards the first team starting a new club era. Owing to financial worries<ref>{{cite web|url=https://elpais.com/diario/1983/09/21/deportes/432943211_850215.html|title=Madrid did pay 750 millions of pesetas|language=es|accessdate=2 July 2020|date=20 September 1983|author=José Damián González}}</ref> Presidente Luis de Carlos with a narrow space for star players transfers in the club,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://elpais.com/diario/1983/09/20/deportes/432856806_850215.html|title=Real Madrid Board treated the club crisis|language=es|accessdate=2 July 2020|date=19 September 1983|author=José Damián González}}</ref> chose to support rejuvenate the squad for this campaign aimed by successful seasons of basque sides [[Real Sociedad]] and [[Athletic Bilbao]] with low profile Spanish players being majority in their squads. However, for the second time the club offered a contract to Brazilian midfielder [[Zico (footballer)|Zico]] being surpassed in the race by [[Udinese Calcio]] which bought him from [[Flamengo]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com.br/futebol/artigo/_/id/7136265/real-madrid-tentou-tirar-zico-o-pele-branco-do-flamengo-duas-vezes-relembra-jornal|title=Real Madrid tentou tirar Zico, o 'Pelé Branco', do Flamengo, duas vezes, relembra jornal|publisher=espn.com.br|date=8 July 2020|accessdate=1 September 2021|language=pt}}</ref>

Shockingly, the team was early eliminated in the [[1983–84 UEFA Cup#First round|UEFA Cup]] first round by Czech underdogs side [[AC Sparta Prague|Sparta Prague]]. Di Stefano managed the team to clinch the first spot of League table for several rounds until March when a 1–1 draw at Pamplona against Osasuna and lost a decisive match at [[San Mamés]] against [[Athletic Bilbao]] with a 0–1 score collapsed its chances to take the title in favor of basque side Athletic Bilbao despite the two teams finished on League table tied on points. Meanwhile, in [[1983–84 Copa del Rey]] the squad was defeated in semi-finals by, again, Athletic Bilbao after a penalty shoot-out series only three days after the basque team took the title away of Real Madrid on a tie-breaker for the second consecutive year.

During May, the squad was early eliminated by [[Atlético Madrid]] in the [[1984 Copa de la Liga]] first round. Forward [[Juanito (footballer, born 1954)|Juanito]] won the [[Pichichi trophy]] with 17 goals scored in League, tied along [[Jorge da Silva]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.laopiniondemalaga.es/opinion/2020/01/15/illa-illa-illa-juanito-maravilla/1138623.html|publisher=La Opinión de Málaga|title=Illa, Illa, Juanito Maravilla|accessdate=2 July 2020|date=15 January 2020|language=es}}</ref> After two years as head coach and no-titles clinched, Argentine head coach [[Alfredo Di Stéfano]] was sacked by President [[Luis de Carlos]] towards the end of campaign.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://elpais.com/diario/1984/07/22/deportes/459295207_850215.html|title=They left me alone in the Plant (Santiago Bernabéu Stadium)|work=El País|date=24 July 1984|accessdate=2 July 2020|language=es}}</ref>
